summary: Two Texas campers/hikers (couple) became hypothermic after camping near Lake Como at 11,765 ft in the Blanca Massif; they hiked up Sunday afternoon unprepared with no layers and a tent without a rain fly, never reached the lake and camped about 1/4 mile short. Emergency call came around 2:35 a.m. Monday amid heavy rain and dangerous flooding/rockfall conditions on Lake Como Road. AVSAR reached them, warmed them with hot water bottles and sugary drinks, and brought them back to safety about 6 hours later; they were checked by medical professionals.
location: Lake Como, Blanca Massif, Sangre de Cristo Range
notes: Discovered via run-131 Monte Vista Journal chunk (rotation pick): the Durango Telegraph "Out in the cold" account and advnture/captainsjournal mirrors all describe the same 2:35 a.m. call and "ignorance kills" AVSAR quote; incident date pinned to Monday June 27, 2022 per the AVSAR release quoted on captainsjournal (published 2022-07-03) — 2022-06-27 was a Monday. The man was vomiting, severely dehydrated, with a headache. Lake Como Road was exceptionally dangerous during the rescue due to heavy rain, rockfall risk and a river running down the road. AVSAR noted the couple had twice declined assistance from SAR crews on the way up. Run 571: AVSAR mission-report URL appended (subagent-opened this run); AVSAR confirms the 2022-06-27 date, 2:35 a.m. call amid flooding/rockfall on Lake Como Road, and 8:22 a.m. trailhead EMS handoff.
